news.title: Bihar ministers discuss new building bylaws for faster approvals
news.para: Bihar's upcoming Building Bylaws for 2026 seek to streamline the approval processes. A high-level group of ministers has scrutinized the draft regulations. This initiative aims to enhance transparency and promote construction throughout the state, supporting critical infrastructure development and boosting economic activities. Ultimately, these proposed bylaws align with the ambitious vision for a progressive Bihar.

news.title: Pimpri Chinchwad civic body likely to record low property tax collection compared to previous two years
news.para: The Pimpri Chinchwad Municipal Corporation predicts a dip in property tax revenues for the upcoming fiscal year. In a bid to enhance collection rates, heightened enforcement actions have been initiated. Political candidates and residents in red zones are responding positively to various incentives offered. To further the recovery process, over eighty non-residential properties have been seized by tax authorities, and water supply cut-offs are being implemented.

news.title: Chandigarh scraps mandatory no-dues certificate for leasehold property sale
news.para: The Chandigarh administration has eliminated the requirement for a no-dues certificate, streamlining the process of selling leasehold properties in the Union Territory. This amendment, championed by the Property Consultants Association Chandigarh, significantly accelerates real estate transactions. As a result, buyers, sellers, and consultants can expect a smoother experience with reduced administrative hold-ups.

news.title: CBI books Essel Group chairman Subhash Chandra, others over alleged ₹1,322 crore LICHFL loan loss
news.para: Subhash Chandra, along with eight others, is under scrutiny as the CBI has registered an FIR accusing them of inflating their net worth to secure loans fraudulently. This situation has led LIC Housing Finance to announce a staggering loss exceeding ₹1,322 crore. The Directorate of Enforcement will also step in with a money laundering investigation, and those accused can expect to be questioned soon about these dubious financial activities.

news.title: SC-appointed team surveys sites in Lucknow for land use violations
news.para: A Supreme Court team conducted a detailed survey of land-use regulations in Lucknow. They focused on properties in Aliganj flagged for regulatory breaches, while also investigating the responses by the Lucknow Development Authority. The inspections encompassed sites in Sarsawan, Gomti Nagar Extension, and Wellness City, with the results to be forwarded to the Supreme Court shortly for their consideration.

news.title: Over 180 MahaRERA recovery warrants worth ₹146.5 crore pending in Pune district; collector sets April deadline
news.para: Pune district collector Jitendra Dudi ordered revenue officials to execute all pending MahaRERA recovery warrants.  He stressed that homebuyers must receive their hard-earned money without further delay.  186 recovery warrant orders totaling Rs146.5 crore remained pending as of January 2026.  Officials will take coercive measures against defaulting developers to meet the April-end deadline.  The district's recovery data will be uploaded to the collectorate website for public transparency.

news.title: Mumbai: For flouting pollution norms, BMC to revoke builders’ project permission
news.para: Responding to escalating air quality concerns, the BMC has implemented tough penalties for construction sites that fail to adopt effective air pollution mitigation strategies. Architects and developers could face suspension of licenses or revocation of development permissions if they do not comply. Additionally, a 100% penalty will be imposed on applicable premium rates for any unauthorized work conducted after a stop-work notice.

news.title: NGT orders Pune builder to pay ₹7.36 crore compensation for construction without environmental clearance
news.para: The National Green Tribunal mandated a Pune developer to pay Rs 7.36 crore as compensation for engaging in construction activities without obtaining the necessary Environmental Clearance. The tribunal distinguished between two project phases for evaluation purposes. Consequently, authorities will assess damages and enforce penalties based on the violation framework, with the compensation allocated for environmental enhancement in the impacted area.

news.title: Labour department gets 10 days to verify crèche compliance at Noida construction sites
news.para: In an effort to protect workers, the district administration has allowed the labour department ten days to conduct inspections of construction sites. This initiative follows a mandate for crèche facilities at any site with fifty or more employees, ensuring that these spaces are clean, safe, and easily reachable. The directive comes in wake of a disturbing rape-murder incident, with heavy penalties for non-compliant developers looming on the horizon.

news.title: Trichy: 49 flats among BWGs told to process their solid waste
news.para: The Trichy corporation has pinpointed 302 properties as significant bulk waste producers. These properties are now required to manage their solid waste autonomously. The local government plans to educate these entities gradually, providing demonstrations on effective waste disposal methods. A meeting is scheduled to establish a concrete timeline for optimizing waste collection processes.

news.title: West Bengal government to develop flats, plots for 3,500 families
news.para: The West Bengal Housing Board is set to launch four new residential projects and will also provide plots for the public. Planned locations include Thakurpukur and two sites in New Town. In addition, a G+7 building aimed at Low and Middle-Income Groups will be erected in Siliguri. Furthermore, residential plots will be cultivated in Binnaguri, Jalpaiguri within the upcoming year.

news.title: Shalimar Corp acquires three-acre  land parcel in Lucknow for ₹450 crore
news.para: Shalimar Corp has acquired a three-acre land parcel in Lucknow for ₹450 crore. This acquisition marks a significant deal within tier two cities.  Developers are actively acquiring land in prime locations due to rising demand.  Consumers now seek planned neighborhoods with quality construction and modern amenities.  This trend indicates a new wave of real estate growth in tier two cities.

news.title: SC isssues notice to Goa, others on plea against Bhutani Infra's project in Sancoale
news.para: The Supreme Court issued a notice to the Goa government concerning a petition from Goa Bachao Abhiyan, targeting the Bhutani Infra's Sancoale project. Previously, the High Court rejected GBA's objections, labeling them unsubstantiated. The organization claims unlawful hill-cutting and faults in project approvals, urging the formation of an independent committee to probe the alleged environmental breaches.

news.title: GIS maps to be attached to sale deeds from October in Maharashtra, rollout in 10 districts in first phase
news.para: Starting in October, Maharashtra is set to revolutionize property transactions by incorporating GIS maps into sale deeds. This innovative shift will replace traditional boundary descriptions with accurate digital coordinates, enhancing transparency in property dealings. The department of land records suggests conducting land measurements in ten districts before registration, aiming to streamline the verification process and minimize disputes and fraudulent activities.

news.title: Greater Noida plot allottees again get two more years to complete construction
news.para: The Greater Noida Authority has granted a two-year extension for plot allottees, pushing the deadline to June 30, 2028. This opportunity allows over five thousand individuals facing construction delays to finalize their projects. However, it is crucial to note that failure to meet this deadline could result in cancellations of their allotments, highlighting the urgency for action after long years of inactivity.

news.title: HERC launches probe into power rule violations in housing societies in Gurugram
news.para: Haryana's electricity regulatory body has initiated a comprehensive investigation into widespread non-compliance regarding electricity supply protocols for group housing societies. The inquiry focuses on potential violations of both single-point supply rules and the use of standardized billing software. DHBVN and the implicated developers are named in the ongoing inquiry, with final conclusions still awaited following additional hearings and submissions.

news.title: Supreme court rejects builder’s challenge to Nagpur STP land acquisition
news.para: The Supreme Court chose not to challenge a High Court decision that confirmed the legality of land acquisition for a sewerage treatment facility linked to a state initiative. The High Court's dismissal of the builder's claims about lapsed reservations stands firm. Importantly, the builder still has the opportunity to seek increased compensation. This verdict reflects progress for critical community infrastructure.

news.title: Flats handed over without completion certificates at Ghaziabad society in flagrant violation of UP Apartment Act: HC
news.para: The Allahabad High Court has mandated that the Ghaziabad Development Authority elucidate its role following claims of violations of the UP Apartment Act by developers. The court raised concerns over the delivery of possession occurring before the issuance of completion certificates. The Authority defended itself, stating that compounding applications have been managed per the relevant bylaws.

news.title: Pranav Constructions raises ₹84 crore from anchor investors ahead of IPO
news.para: Pranav Constructions Ltd has raised Rs 84.24 crore from anchor investors ahead of its initial public offering (IPO). Shares were allocated at Rs 124 each. This IPO, which includes a fresh issue and an offer-for-sale component, will be open for subscription starting September 7. The company is primarily focused on redevelopment projects within Mumbai's western suburbs.

news.title: About 800 buildings in Odisha face fire safety violation notices; special drive from September 15
news.para: Cracking down on fire safety violations, the Odisha Fire and Emergency Service (OFES) has issued notices to around 800 buildings allegedly operating without mandatory fire safety certificates and will launch a month-long statewide enforcement and awareness drive from Sept 15 to improve compliance and strengthen preparedness.
